rationale: The integrated diff removes the split request/response mixin architecture and consolidates those responsibilities into the concrete Request and Response classes. Former base and mixin modules become compatibility shims, while dependent imports and inheritance are redirected. This is a large verified responsibility and inheritance redesign.

The integrated diff extracts protocol-independent request and response behavior into new Sans-IO base classes. Existing WSGI Request and Response classes lose hundreds of lines and inherit from those new bases, establishing a new dependency direction and responsibility boundary.

The integrated diff removes the multipart state machine and low-level parsing responsibility from formparser.py, introduces a Sans-IO event-driven MultipartDecoder/Encoder subsystem, and rewires form parsing and test encoding to consume that abstraction. This is a verified module responsibility extraction.

The integrated diff moves host trust and URL construction responsibility out of WSGI-specific helpers into Sans-IO utilities and the Sans-IO request base, then converts WSGI functions to adapters. Existing request inheritance and dependency direction are changed accordingly.

The integrated diff extracts request-independent HTTP parsing and resource-modification logic from http.py into a new Sans-IO HTTP module with explicit arguments, and redirects Sans-IO Request to it. This is a verified responsibility and dependency-boundary extraction.

The integrated diff moves content-length, query-string, path-info, script-name, and path-extraction algorithms from WSGI-specific code into Sans-IO utilities, leaving WSGI adapters around the extracted functions. This is a verified responsibility and dependency-direction change.

The integrated diff deletes the 3,040-line monolithic datastructures.py and redistributes its responsibilities into dedicated accept, authorization, cache-control, file-storage, header, mixin, range, and structure modules behind a package export surface. This is a direct module decomposition and dependency redesign.

Every integrated production hunk replaces TYPE_CHECKING-only imports from wsgiref.types with equivalent _typeshed.wsgi imports. Runtime code, module responsibility, inheritance, dependencies, and state ownership are unchanged.

The integrated diff enables stricter typing and applies annotations, casts, formatting, dead compatibility cleanup, and localized correctness adjustments across existing modules. Review found no production responsibility extraction, module decomposition, inheritance redesign, or state-ownership transfer; its breadth must not itself become a risk label.

The integrated diff adds typing annotations and removes or reformats local compatibility and debugging helpers across existing modules. It does not create a new production subsystem, move responsibility between modules, redirect dependency ownership, or redesign inheritance/state ownership.
The integrated production diff only changes deprecation-removal version text from 2.4 to 3.0 across existing APIs. Runtime structure and ownership are unchanged.

The integrated diff removes previously deprecated parameters, aliases, properties, and compatibility branches from their existing modules. It is API cleanup for a major release; review found no responsibility transfer, new module boundary, or replacement architectural abstraction.
The integrated production diff removes residual Python 2 comparison and compatibility methods from existing classes. It is compatibility cleanup without a responsibility or dependency redesign.

The integrated production hunks are localized cleanup, documentation, signature compatibility, and condition simplification in five existing modules. No responsibility or dependency moves between them.
The integrated diff adopts postponed annotation evaluation and adjusts annotations across existing modules. This is typing modernization, not runtime architectural restructuring.
The integrated diff tightens numeric parsing and validation in existing HTTP and form-processing paths. It is behavior correction without moving responsibilities or changing module architecture.
The integrated production changes correct comments, docstrings, and messages in existing modules. There is no structural runtime change.
The integrated diff deprecates bytes and charset API paths and updates call sites inside existing modules. It is staged API cleanup, not a transfer of architectural responsibility.
The integrated diff adds send_from_directory beside the existing send_file utility in the same module. It is a new utility capability, not a refactor or responsibility movement.
The integrated production diff adds explicit exception chaining at existing error boundaries. Module responsibilities and dependency direction are unchanged.
The integrated production diff deletes unreachable compatibility code from safe_str_cmp. It is local dead-code removal.
The integrated diff adds an update method to the existing Headers data structure. It is a local API feature with unchanged ownership.
The integrated production diff handles a double-leading-slash path in the existing development server. It is localized behavior correction.
The integrated diff adds two response-header descriptors using the established header-property machinery. It is an API feature rather than architectural restructuring.
The integrated production changes replace BinaryIO annotations with IO[bytes] for typing compatibility. Runtime architecture is unchanged.
The integrated diff makes the existing test-client response close its input stream. Resource cleanup changes locally without moving responsibility between modules.

The integrated diff removes a large custom traceback representation and rendering layer, delegates traceback traversal to Python's traceback module, and rewires debugger consumers to the reduced interface. This is removal and redirection of a production subsystem responsibility.
The integrated production diff replaces os.path.sep with os.sep at two call sites. It has no architectural effect.
The integrated production diff converts one cache-control value to int in the existing property path. It is a localized correctness fix.
The integrated diff changes tests only and contains no production architectural change.
The integrated diff removes the bundled demonstration test application and its secret binary fixture. It does not move or redesign Werkzeug's runtime architecture.
The integrated diff changes documentation only.
The integrated production diff wraps IPv6 server names in brackets in the existing Sans-IO utility. It is a localized correctness fix.
The integrated diff removes a legacy IRI redirect workaround from existing URL and response paths. It is compatibility cleanup, not a subsystem responsibility transfer.
The integrated production diff corrects IPv6 scope formatting in the existing serving logger. It is a localized logging fix.

The integrated diff redesigns Authorization and WWWAuthenticate from dict-mixin data holders into explicit parameter-or-token domain objects, moves header parsing and serialization behind those objects, and rewires request and response integration. This is a substantial authentication subsystem boundary and state-ownership refactor.

The integrated diff removes the urllib CookieJar adapter layer, consolidates cookie parsing and serialization, and gives the Werkzeug test client ownership of explicit cookie state and domain/path matching. This is a subsystem state-management and responsibility redesign rather than a localized behavior fix.

The integrated diff retires Werkzeug's internal URL abstraction in favor of urllib.parse across routing, requests, serving, middleware, form parsing, tests, utilities, and responses while turning werkzeug.urls into a compatibility boundary. This is a broad dependency-direction and responsibility migration.

The integrated diff deprecates OrderedMultiDict aliases while preserving their implementation through private compatibility names. It is API lifecycle cleanup without moving a runtime responsibility or redesigning a dependency boundary.
The integrated diff fixes accepted HTTP q-value forms by replacing one private float parser with a local regular expression. It is a localized parsing correction.
The integrated diff deprecates the package __version__ attribute and obtains the server version through importlib metadata. It is API lifecycle and metadata cleanup, not a subsystem redesign.

The integrated diff replaces digit prechecks with int conversion and error handling at existing call sites. It is broad correctness cleanup but does not move responsibilities or change module boundaries.
The integrated production diff changes one macOS help message. It has no architectural effect.
The integrated diff drops Python 3.7 and mechanically replaces compatibility typing imports and syntax. It does not transfer a production responsibility or redesign a dependency boundary.

The integrated diff replaces html.escape calls with MarkupSafe escaping at existing HTML-rendering call sites. This is a dependency substitution for escaping semantics, not a movement of the rendering responsibilities themselves.

The integrated diff restores default cookie paths and corrects case-insensitive cookie attribute parsing within the existing cookie implementation. It is a behavior fix following the earlier subsystem refactor.
The integrated diff makes small Python 3.12 compatibility substitutions in authentication, resource loading, and generated routing AST nodes. It preserves the existing architecture.

The integrated diff adds a compatibility helper to preserve invalid itms-services redirect URLs and routes existing response handling through it. It is a targeted behavior workaround, not an architectural redesign.
The integrated production diff sends the final empty multipart data event so empty test uploads are encoded correctly. It is a one-line correctness fix.
The integrated diff reorders existing iri_to_uri compatibility checks so passing bytes warns instead of failing. It is localized compatibility behavior.
The integrated diff stops applying the multipart part-count limit to URL-encoded form data. It is a localized form-parser correctness fix.

The integrated diff revises and deprecates extension points inside the existing FormDataParser and updates its Request wiring, but parsing responsibility remains in the same module and class family. Under the strict rubric this is API refactoring, not a module, dependency-direction, inheritance, or state-ownership redesign.
The integrated diff escapes control characters in the existing development-server request logger. It is a localized security hardening fix.
